statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band as NQ futures hold a 38-point overnight range after the record Nasdaq-100 close faded off its session high.
recommendation: Tail at 10% maps to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The published forecast carries a WATCH band across the 17:00-20:00 UTC sequence on 7 October covering the 10-year note auction and the September FOMC minutes, where Tail is modelled conditionally at 20-23%.
headline: NQ holds a 38-point overnight range after the record Nasdaq-100 close; Tail stays low into the September FOMC minutes
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at a record 31,224.69, up 148.24 points or 0.48%, alongside record closes for the S&P 500 at 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq Composite. The session peaked at 31,361.37 and then faded roughly 137 points to finish near its 31,208.20 low. Overnight, December NQ futures trade 31,499.75, up 16.50 points or 0.05%, inside a 38-point band of 31,483.25-31,521.00. That observed retracement into the close followed by an unusually tight Globex range is the direct opposite of the no-retracement structure Tail measures, so Tail is assessed at 10%. Asian cash trade is mixed and orderly, with the Nikkei 225 up 0.17%, the Hang Seng up 1.00%, the Shanghai Composite up 0.31%, the KOSPI up 0.06% and the ASX 200 down 0.37%, and VIX settled at 15.01, down 3.29%. Stress is held at 45% because the environment beneath the record prints remains genuinely difficult. The 30-year yield sits near 5.66% and the 10-year near 5.31%, both at levels last seen in 2002, and the long end has been driven by energy-linked inflation concerns, a deteriorating fiscal picture and weak bond buybacks. Brent is back above 101 dollars and WTI above 90 dollars, recovering from five-week lows while the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed on its 220th day, with nine UKMTO-reported tanker attacks already this month even as Middle East crude exports have climbed above their pre-war average. Leadership is narrow: Nvidia and AMD printed fresh all-time highs with Nvidia approaching a six trillion dollar market capitalisation, Marvell gained about 8% on a raised fiscal-2028 revenue target and Constellation Energy rose roughly 13% on a 4.3 billion dollar Google nuclear agreement, yet only about 25% of S&P 500 members trade above their 50-day averages. The dominant mode is recorded as mixed: the daily trend is up, while the close faded to the lower end of the session range and the overnight band is two-way. The principal checkpoint inside the forecast window is the release of the September FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on 7 October, confirmed on the Federal Reserve's own October calendar and preceded by a 10-year note auction at 17:00 UTC. Because October hike odds have fallen from roughly 70% to about 20% since that 25 basis point hike to 3.75-4.00%, a hawkish minutes read remains a credible repricing mechanism, and the forecast therefore carries a conditional WATCH band from 17:00 to 20:00 UTC rather than a block. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale, dated 29 September, with a partial collection status, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 8-12% through the Asian and European hours of 6 October, rose to a 22% peak at 15:00 UTC as the U.S. session extended, with the 15:00 and 16:00 UTC slots mapping to WATCH, then decayed to 11% by 23:00 UTC as the index faded off its high into the close. Stress held in a narrow 45-48% band throughout and Confidence stayed at 86-88%, while dominant mode shifted from mixed to trend-up during the U.S. session and back to mixed after the fade.
outlookSummary: Remaining Asian and European hours are modelled with Tail at 9-13% on contained two-way ranges. Tail lifts to 16-17% across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the first cash hours for opening-range expansion, then to a conditional 20-23% WATCH band from the 17:00 UTC 10-year note auction through the 18:00 UTC September FOMC minutes and the following power hour. Risk decays to 11-16% after the 20:00 UTC cash close. Stress tracks Tail higher to a 53% peak around the minutes, and Confidence eases from 87% to 85% as live price-path evidence ages. No post-event price structure is treated as observed.
